newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka launches multiple attacks on rebel base.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka launches multiple attacks on rebel base.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces launched air, naval and artillery strikes on Tamil rebel jungle bases in the northeast on Thursday to disrupt guerrilla preparations for an attack, military officials said.
"It was a well-coordinated, pre-emptive strike on all LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) bases in the area," a navy spokesman told Reuters.
"An LTTE buildup for an attack was reported in the area. Our attacks should disrupt their plans and also cause heavy casualties."
The rebels were believed to have suffered casualties and were calling for reinforcements, according to rebel radio traffic intercepted by the army, military officials said.
The attacks were centred on the LTTE's so-called "14 base" complex in the jungles of northeastern Mullaitivu district, 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo, the officials said.
"LTTE camps in the area were pounded for three or four hours starting at dawn," an official said. Bases for the rebels' Sea Tiger naval wing were also attacked.
LTTE rebels overran a key military base in the area last year, killing or capturing more than 1,000 soldiers in the army's worst setback of the war, now in its 14th year.
Military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said the aim of Thursday's offensive was to destroy all known rebel bases in the Mullaitivu jungles and along the eastern seaboard.
"Air force pilots have reported direct hits on targets," he told Reuters.
Several camps in the base complex and others on the coast were destroyed, he said.
A LTTE spokesman in London confirmed the attack but said the Sri Lankan military shelled Tamil villages and not rebel camps.
"This is not an attack on any LTTE base at all. This is a deliberate attack on Tamil villages in the area by the armed forces," Anton Rajah told Reuters by telephone.
He said air force bombers attacked Tamil villages in the Mullaitivu district. "It is feared many human lives have been lost but further information on casualties is not immeditely available."
Jayatunga declined comment on reports that troops from the Weli Oya army base, about 40 km (25 miles) south of Mullaitivu, were advancing on the "14 base" stronghold.
"Ground troops are there in certain locations in the area but we can't say where," he said.
An air force spokesman said Kfir fighter jets and Pucara ground attack planes were deployed.
"We took some targets given by army intelligence in the 14 base area," he said.
Thursday's attack by the military comes after the LTTE overran an army detachment in the eastern Batticaloa district last week, killing at least 65 soldiers.
The military said at least 200 rebels were killed in the raid.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
